title: Principles of Accounting, Volume 2: Managerial Accounting
source_classification: Open educational textbook; managerial accounting instruction, not standard-setting authority
questions: Job/process cost-object and accumulation choices
ABC activities, pools and drivers
standard cost cards and material/labor/overhead variances
contribution margin and variable/fixed cost decision use
inspected_summary: The public textbook distinguishes job costing (trace identifiable direct cost to a unique job/service) from process costing (accumulate by department/process for homogeneous continuous output); hybrid approaches are possible and information detail should justify collection cost. Its ABC chapter explains activity pools and multiple drivers where one volume base poorly reflects overhead consumption. Its standard-cost chapters explain planned input price/quantity and labor rate/time comparisons, flexible budgets, variable overhead rate and efficiency variances, and fixed-overhead spending/production-volume variances. The contribution-margin chapter defines sales less variable costs as the amount available for fixed costs and profit. This is educational managerial guidance; it does not establish GAAP policy or require management to allocate every fixed cost to a product.
